I have been working this land for 35 years. My body is not what it was, and my son works in the city now, so I plan carefully to not overwork myself. I know this soil. I know when it needs water just by looking at the leaves.

I will split my 5 mu roughly — 2 mu for cotton, 3 mu for spring maize. Cotton earns more per mu but takes more out of me. Maize I can mostly manage with machine help from the village.

For cotton, I switched to Bt seed years ago and never went back. The bollworm used to eat everything before. I still spray a few times for aphids and spider mites, but not like the old days. I water it maybe three times — before flowering, during boll set, and once if August is dry. I don't waste water. The well costs money to run.

For spring maize, I use hybrid seed — everyone does, it yields much better. I put down compound fertilizer at planting and top-dress with urea when it's knee-high. I irrigate four times because spring in Quzhou is dry and the grain-fill period needs moisture. I'll spray once or twice if I see corn borer or aphids.

I use rotary tillage for both — I hire the machine from the village service. My back can't handle deep ploughing anymore.
